external_invariants: Model is the pretrained microsoft/resnet-18 loaded from the local request['assets'] directory only (from_pretrained with local_files_only=True), 11,689,512 parameters, with its classification head producing full 1000-class logits.

Precision policy is FP32 everywhere: weights loaded with dtype=torch.float32; TF32 disabled for both torch.backends.cuda.matmul and torch.backends.cudnn; cudnn.benchmark=False; torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'). No AMP, quantization, autocast or reduced-precision path may be introduced.
Deterministic setup policies from common.configure(): torch.set_num_threads(4), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1), torch.manual_seed(20261020).

The workload input is exactly pixels = images[torch.arange(batch, device=device) % images.shape[0]].contiguous(), where images is the (3,3,224,224) float32 NCHW tensor loaded from assets pixels.npy; batch comes from request['workload']['batch'] (32 for this frozen request), never an embedded constant.

The measured invocation is a single complete forward model(pixel_values=pixels).logits executed under @torch.inference_mode(), with the model in eval() mode; no training, gradients, optimizer, sampling or communication exists in the workload.

Quality fidelity checks that bound any optimization: full logits must satisfy assert_close against the reference with atol=rtol=1e-4, and integer top-1 labels must match exactly (torch.equal on argmax(-1) over all 1000 classes, require_exact_top1); the +1 corruption negative control must remain rejected. No accuracy or convergence claim beyond this reference fidelity.

latency_ms is the per-batch-call wall latency of that one forward at fixed batch=32, and images_per_second = batch*1e9/elapsed_ns is its exact reciprocal; no performance constraint is attached to latency_ms for this request (the workloads.json images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio=0.95 constraint belongs to the offline row's peak_allocated_bytes memory goal).

The adapter must use context['device'] (the worker-bound CUDA device) for the model, input tensors and device placement instead of choosing a physical GPU, and must not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time.

Statistics queries (max_memory_allocated) stay in metrics() outside the timer; run() must not duplicate the framework's synchronize/peak-reset boundary operations because the source has no internal completion point.

The online (batch=1) workload row and the held-out unseen_batch (batch=7) workload in workloads.json are not part of this frozen request; other workload variants would supply a different batch through the same adapter.

selection.rationale: The accepted BN-fold bundle (trial-d2a4cb48d3, objective 4.181 ms vs parent 4.227 ms, quality pass) made the measured single batch=32 FP32 forward GPU-bound: in the current-revision execution_timeline capture the kernel active union is 3989.5 us inside a 4071.0 us span with only 81.5 us of launch gaps, and python_runtime shows host self-time ~0 with the wall dominated by cuda_synchronize, so only kernel-time reduction can move latency_ms. The fold also left a measurable pointwise-epilogue tax around the convolutions themselves (call-resources.json, revision 353b783e): every one of the 20 folded conv sites (17 ResNetConvLayer + 3 ResNetShortCut calls) emits an extra non-vectorized broadcast bias-add kernel because the eager cudnn path applies conv bias as a separate elementwise pass (20 kernels, 355.9 us total; the stem site fad32b28bd6e0def6ce7593e alone pays 206.6 us after its 262.4 us conv), plus 17 separate aten::relu kernels (350.9 us) and 8 residual aten::add_ kernels (77.3 us). That is ~784 us of epilogue traffic against 2974 us of actual conv kernels (scudnn/winograd/implicit_sgemm). These kernels live entirely inside the 17 ResNetConvLayer, 3 ResNetShortCut and 8 ResNetBasicLayer module boundaries (modeling_resnet.py:113-136: layer[0] conv+ReLU, layer[1] conv with activation=None, then hidden += residual, final ReLU), which is the coherent editable boundary for fusing bias and ReLU into the conv/residual epilogues. The 8 previously selected conv/shortcut groups are re-selected so the new joint bundle explicitly supersedes the whole inherited fold bundle at every site it declared, transferring its required-call coverage to the new replacements instead of composing under them.
selection.hypothesis: Re-executing the same FP32 math with fused epilogues removes most of the 707 us of bias-add plus ReLU kernel time: (a) at the 9 ReLU-terminated conv sites, run conv+bias+ReLU as one fused execution (aten::cudnn_convolution_relu / cudnn fused bias-activation path; verified to exist in the worker torch 2.13.0+cu129 op registry) eliminating the broadcast bias-add and the separate ReLU; (b) at the 8 activation=None second convs and 3 shortcuts, emit conv without bias and carry the folded bias into a single fused residual epilogue at the owning ResNetBasicLayer boundary that computes ReLU(hidden + residual + b_conv2 + b_shortcut) in one vectorized kernel, replacing conv2's bias-add, the shortcut's bias-add, the add_ and the post-add ReLU. Expected ceiling ~0.6-0.7 ms of the 4.06 ms GPU time (up to ~16%), i.e. clean latency_ms from ~4.18 toward ~3.5-3.6; a partial outcome (only per-site fused bias+ReLU pointwise) still yields ~0.15-0.35 ms. Numerics are unchanged in exact arithmetic (same FP32 adds/ReLU, TF32 off, cudnn.benchmark off, no AMP/quantization), so assert_close at 1e-4 and exact top-1 against the reference should hold; if the fused cudnn path is unavailable or slower on any shape, the replacement falls back to the parent callable and keeps the accepted behavior. This is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework's A/B measurement, not a predicted acceptance.

proposal.rationale: Repair of the concrete failure documented in inputs/previous-feedback.txt: the accepted BN-fold bundle (trial-d2a4cb48d3, paired win only ~46 us of the ~428 us of removed cudnn::bn_fw_inf kernels) left the eager cudnn path paying every folded conv bias as a separate NON-VECTORIZED broadcast elementwise kernel (call-resources.json revision 353b783e: 20 add kernels, 355.9 us total, 206.6 us alone after the stem conv on the [32,64,112,112] output; grid 100352x128 unvectorized CUDAFunctor_add), plus 17 separate aten::relu kernels (350.9 us) and 8 residual aten::add_ kernels (77.3 us) - ~784 us of pointwise epilogue traffic against ~2974 us of conv kernels, on an invocation the current execution_timeline shows GPU-compute-bound (kernel active union 3989.5 us inside a 4071.0 us span, 81.5 us launch gaps, host self-time ~0). Only kernel-time removal can move latency_ms. This joint bundle explicitly replaces the whole accepted fold bundle at every site it declared (17 ResNetConvLayer + 3 ResNetShortCut module calls) and additionally takes over the 8 ResNetBasicLayer boundaries (groups 5233e425bbe8203a4dc0, 5eb0dee1d36938317bbe, c1271430eda49ac23557, 9f7c0638f7c2fd3e7c50), transferring required-call coverage to these replacements: (a) the 9 ReLU-terminated conv sites (stem fad32b28bd6e0def6ce7593e + the 8 layer.0 first convs) execute the BN-folded conv as ONE aten::cudnn_convolution_relu kernel (registered CUDA kernel verified in the worker torch 2.13.0+cu129 registry; the production ConvReLU2d fused path using cudnnConvolutionBiasActivationForward), eliminating the broadcast bias-add and the separate ReLU at those sites; (b) the 8 activation=None second convs and 3 shortcut convs emit the folded conv with bias=None (one conv kernel, no elementwise bias pass) when invoked inside their owning basic layer's fused window and hand the folded bias to the owner; (c) each ResNetBasicLayer replacement still calls its real child module boundaries (self.layer Sequential and self.shortcut, including the 5 nn.Identity shortcuts) so ALL 28 declared replacements execute on every invocation with no counter-filling dummy work, then computes ReLU(hidden + residual + b_conv2 + b_shortcut) as ONE vectorized Triton kernel (eager relu(x+r+b) fallback if Triton is unavailable), replacing conv2's bias-add, the shortcut's bias-add, the add_ and the post-add ReLU. Coordination is fail-safe: a per-physical-module window marker decides bias-free emission, and the epilogue adds back exactly the biases the children reported as not applied, so any guard rejection or per-site runtime failure (including the fused cudnn op raising on a specific shape, per-site sticky fallback to conv+bias then activation) degrades to the accepted bundle's behavior with unchanged outputs. Numerics are the same FP32 adds/ReLU in a different association order (relu(x_nobias + r + b_sum) vs relu((x_nobias+b2)+(r+bsc))): CPU pre-validation with the frozen weights, the exact fold arithmetic, all 28 replacements installed and the full batch=32 fixture input reproduces the 1000-class logits with max_abs_err=7.63e-6 (bound: atol=rtol=1e-4, prior accepted fold itself measured 9.5e-6 on GPU, reference top1-top2 margin 0.1446), exact top-1 preserved, bit-stable across repeated runs; guard fallbacks (grad enabled) return outputs bit-identical to the parent path, and standalone conv2/shortcut invocation outside the fused window reproduces the parent site output within 4.8e-6. Expected effect: removes up to ~0.70 ms of pointwise kernel time (355.9 us bias-adds + 350.9 us relus + 77.3 us add_) and adds back ~0.08-0.12 ms of Triton epilogue traffic (one 3-tensor pass over the 8 layer outputs, ~96 MB total) plus ~0 for the cudnn bias/relu epilogues, targeting latency_ms ~4.18 -> ~3.5-3.7 with images_per_second (exact reciprocal) rising proportionally; peak_allocated_bytes stays at the accepted fold's level (folded copies replace that bundle's, one epilogue output replaces the old relu output). These are hypotheses the framework's paired A/B must confirm, not predicted acceptance; launch-register data is not treated as occupancy or causal evidence. Eliminated inner calls are all inside replaced boundaries and their consumers receive identical values from the fused kernels: the 9 conv1/stem aten::conv2d functional sites are superseded by the fused conv+bias+relu op, the 9 conv-site ReLU module sites and their 9 aten::relu children are applied inside that op, the 8 conv2 Identity activation sites and the 8 ResNetBasicLayer-final ReLU module sites with their 8 aten::relu children and 8 aten::add_ residual sites are computed by the single fused epilogue kernel. The Sequential layer sites, the 5 Identity shortcut sites and the 8 conv2/shortcut aten::conv2d sites keep executing (now bias-free conv). previous-feedback.txt otherwise changes this attempt by ruling out host-side and launch-gap strategies (GPU-bound invocation), by supplying the per-site kernel evidence that motivated exactly these epilogue fusions, and by warning that reference counters only observe declared boundaries - hence children are invoked through their real module callables.

setup_work.description: One-time work at build/installation, outside the timed invocation; no model parameters or BN buffers are modified.
steps: Exact eval-mode BN fold of all 20 conv/BN pairs (scale=gamma/sqrt(running_var+eps), W'=W*scale, b'=beta-scale*running_mean) into contiguous FP32 CUDA copies, folded once per physical conv module and shared between the conv site replacement and its owning basic layer (~11.2M params, ~45 MB; replaces the superseded bundle's folded copies).
Per-channel epilogue bias tensors: zeros(C), b_conv2, b_shortcut (3 sites) and b_conv2+b_shortcut sums; negligible size.

Synthetic-device probes on the leased worker GPU at install (no fixture data): a 1x3x4x8 cudnn_convolution_relu correctness probe against relu(center-tap conv) and a 1x8x2x4 Triton epilogue probe checked against the eager formula; a failed probe latches the eager/two-op fallback paths before the first invocation.

Lazy Triton JIT compilation of the single fp32 add+bias+relu kernel on the first quality invocations (one compile, cached for all 8 layers and all later invocations; worst case a few hundred ms inside the untimed quality/warmup phase, well within the 900 s worker timeout).
setup_work.setup_memory: Folded weight/bias copies ~45 MB allocated during installation and retained for the warm-model lifetime (same footprint class as the superseded fold bundle; reported by lifecycle counters, not by the per-run peak_allocated_bytes reset). No CUDA Graph pools, no persistent runtime buffers beyond the [C] bias vectors.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: Inference-only: replacements are stateless per invocation apart from the per-module coordination marker (reset in a finally block around each child call window) and sticky per-site fallback latches; adapter.reset()/eval() semantics unaffected; no parameter updates, no gradients (guards reject grad-enabled calls to the parent).

quality_risks: cudnn_convolution_relu may pick a different conv algorithm for some shapes (cudnn.benchmark=False heuristics), shifting FP32 rounding; bounded by the 1e-4 tolerance against the 7.63e-6 CPU-validated error and the 0.1446 top1-top2 margin, but only the framework's independent GPU quality check confirms it.

If the fused cudnn op raises on a specific real shape despite the install probe passing, that site sticky-falls back to folded conv+bias followed by the unchanged activation module: correct output, partial speed loss, visible via the folded_conv_relu_two_op route label.
If Triton compilation fails in the worker, all 8 epilogues use the eager relu(x+r+b) path: correct output, ~0.1 ms less benefit, visible via basic_fused_epilogue_eager labels.

Bias re-association (x+r+b_sum vs (x+b2)+(r+bsc)) adds FP32 rounding of the same magnitude as the accepted fold (measured 7.63e-6 max on full logits in CPU pre-validation); the negative control and exact top-1 are re-verified by the framework, not assumed.

Coordinated bias-free conv2/shortcut emission is only consumed by the owning basic-layer replacement's epilogue; every other caller (guard rejection, framework reference invocation, standalone call) gets the full parent-faithful output because the marker window is closed - validated in CPU pre-validation with bit-identical fallback outputs.

Coverage: all 28 declared replacements execute on every invocation through real module boundaries (children are called via self.layer/self.shortcut, not reimplemented in place), so required-call coverage does not depend on eliminated inner functional sites.

unavailable_fields.communication.nccl_algorithm_protocol_ch: Single-device task with distributed_backend=null; observations.json reports communication=not_applicable (reason: single-device task), so nccl_tuning has no collectives to observe and kernel names alone cannot identify protocol.
unavailable_fields.communication.collective_reference_timin: No collectives exist in the measured invocation; collective_calibration's synthetic full-world SUM allreduce is inapplicable to this single-GPU workload.
unavailable_fields.cross_rank_clock_alignment: Single rank; observations.json cross_rank reports no matched pairs and forbids subtracting timestamps from different rank clocks.
unavailable_fields.per_transfer_pcie_nvlink_bytes: No peer transfers in the measured invocation (GPU-resident batch, host-to-device input transfer excluded per request.json notes); device_telemetry provides device-wide NVML rates with native windows only, and PCIe/NVLink traffic must not be inferred from logical payload or memcpy sizes.
unavailable_fields.gpu_readiness_and_consumer_completion_bo: execution_timeline reports clock alignment bounds for matching CPU submissions only; GPU readiness and consumer completion may remain unknown.
unavailable_fields.gpu_compute_durations_from_cprofile: python_runtime runs a perturbing warmed cProfile; its inclusive/self times are host-side dispatch/binding costs, not clean performance scores or GPU compute durations.
unavailable_fields.binding_per_group_cost: evaluation.json setup shows requested binding 'legacy' but effective 'direct' with reason 'no functional replacements', so there is no binding wrapper overhead to isolate; binding_cost would report whole-invocation cost only and is not selected.

plan.rationale: Single-device batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 inference task (observations.json: communication not_applicable, 'single-device task'), so nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and per-collective device_telemetry dimensions are out of scope. The torch collector already ran; its coverage.json shows complete attribution (88/88 cuda_kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous_forward_sequences, 0 autograd_ranges), 0 framework_fallbacks and 0 reference_invocations, so nsys adds nothing for attribution, graph tracing or overlap on this sequential single-stream workload. The accepted candidate 3d785af12... measures 3.45531 ms vs paired parent 4.150355 ms with quality pass and no constraints violated; the remaining observed uncertainty for further latency reduction is whether the residual ~3.46 ms invocation is host-dispatch/binding-bound or device-busy. execution_timeline supplies CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization points, per-device intervals and clock alignment bounds to separate submit-side gaps from device-busy time; python_runtime's warmed cProfile attributes host dispatch and binding call costs. binding_cost is not selected because effective binding is 'direct' with 'no functional replacements' (no additive wrapper overhead to isolate) and the clean paired measurement already attributes the improvement to the candidate. Both selected collectors run on this exact candidate in separate workers; gradient post-accumulate callbacks are not requested (pure inference under inference_mode, 0 autograd ranges).
